prompt: A customer asks Quitanda for every piece of data it holds about her. Which part of a catalogue answers "where is it"?

choices.text: The Data Map
choices.why: Right. Classifications then say which of those columns hold her CPF.

choices.text: The glossary
choices.why: Glossary terms define business words; they do not list where data is stored.

choices.text: Sensitivity labels
choices.why: A label states how to treat data already found; it does not find it.

choices.text: The integration runtime
choices.why: The runtime is where a scan runs, not where its findings are kept.

prompt: A colleague searches "Purview" and finds pages about labelling e-mails and preventing data loss in Microsoft 365. What explains it?
hint: The name covers more than one family.

choices.text: The Data Map scans e-mail by default
choices.why: The Data Map scans registered data sources; mail belongs to the other family.

choices.text: Two product families share the name
choices.why: Right. The two share a portal and sensitivity labels, and the documentation mixes them.

choices.text: They are outdated pages about Azure Data Catalog
choices.why: Azure Data Catalog was a data catalogue; it never labelled e-mails.

choices.text: Search results from another vendor
choices.why: Both families carry Microsoft's own name for them.

prompt: Why does the lesson call a catalogue "a list kept up to date by a machine rather than by memory"?
hint: Each copy was a sensible decision when it was made.

choices.text: Because people are not allowed to edit a catalogue
choices.why: People curate the catalogue; the machine fills the inventory.

choices.text: Copies outpace anyone's notes
choices.why: Right. Quitanda's customer is in the database, the export, Delta tables and Capture files.

choices.text: Because the LGPD requires an automated catalogue
choices.why: The lesson does not say the law requires a tool; it says the request turns into a search.

choices.text: Because scans are free
choices.why: Scans are billed by the processing they use.

prompt: A scan of Quitanda's lake fails to read any file. Which permission does Microsoft's documentation have the Purview account's identity hold on a storage account?

choices.text: Owner
choices.why: Far more than reading needs; a catalogue only has to read.

choices.text: Storage Blob Data Reader
choices.why: Right, which makes the Purview account one of the most privileged readers in the company.

choices.text: Storage Blob Data Contributor, so that it can write the classifications into each blob
choices.why: Classifications are written into the Data Map, not into the source.

choices.text: None, because Purview reads through Azure Resource Manager
choices.why: Resource Manager is the control plane; reading blobs is the data plane and needs a data role.

prompt: Quitanda's SQL Server runs in its own data centre, unreachable from the internet. Where does the scan of it run?
hint: The same idea as Data Factory's runtimes.

choices.text: On Microsoft's own runtime in Azure, through the database's public address
choices.why: There is no public address to reach.

choices.text: Inside Purview's managed resource group
choices.why: That group holds resources Purview creates for itself; it is not inside Quitanda's data centre.

choices.text: On a self-hosted integration runtime installed on a machine there
choices.why: Right. It reaches the source from inside and reports to Purview.

choices.text: Nowhere: Purview scans Azure sources only
choices.why: The self-hosted runtime exists for sources in your own data centre.

prompt: Quitanda draws its collection tree to mirror its org chart. What does the lesson warn about?

choices.text: Teams reorganise faster than data moves
choices.why: Right, and each reorganisation then moves permissions and assets around the tree.

choices.text: Collections cannot be nested more than two levels
choices.why: The lesson describes a tree under a root; it names no depth limit.

choices.text: Permissions granted on a collection are not inherited
choices.why: They are inherited by the collections below, which is why the shape matters.

choices.text: Collections are billed per collection
choices.why: The bill is capacity and scanning, not collections.

prompt: `terraform validate` accepted `azurerm_purview_account`. Where would Quitanda declare the nightly scan of its lake?
hint: What is an Azure resource in this provider, and what is not?

choices.text: In another block of the same file, as `azurerm_purview_scan`
choices.why: Scans are not resources of this provider; they live inside Purview.

choices.text: In Purview itself
choices.why: Right. Terraform declares the account; sources, collections and scans are configured in it.

choices.text: In the storage account's lifecycle rules
choices.why: Lifecycle rules move or delete blobs; they do not scan.

choices.text: In `identity`, which schedules the account's work
choices.why: `identity` gives the account the managed identity scans read with.

prompt: The `tracking` column held eleven-digit numbers. Why did `classify.py` not label it as CPF?

choices.text: Its name does not say CPF
choices.why: The program looks at data, not column names.

choices.text: None of them passed the check digits
choices.why: Right: ten looked like CPFs, none passed.

choices.text: Numbers without dots and a dash do not match the pattern
choices.why: They did: all ten looked like it, and the pattern makes the dots optional.

choices.text: The threshold is 60 and it reached 50
choices.why: It reached 0 per cent once the validator ran.

prompt: The `notes` column held one real CPF in ten rows and was not labelled. What does that show?

choices.text: The validator rejected the CPF
choices.why: It passed: 1 looked like it, 1 passed.

choices.text: Free text is skipped by classifiers
choices.why: The program read the column and found the CPF; the threshold decided.

choices.text: The threshold labels columns that are mostly CPF, so a stray one in free text goes unlabelled
choices.why: Right, which is how personal data hides in a catalogue that looks complete.

choices.text: CPFs in notes are not personal data
choices.why: A CPF is personal data wherever it is typed.

prompt: With `THRESHOLD = 0.6`, how many of a column's 10 sampled rows must pass a rule for the column to be labelled?
hint: The share must be at least the threshold.

prompt: Quitanda sets every custom rule's threshold to 10 per cent so that no stray CPF is missed. What will happen to its catalogue?
hint: Think about any column where one value in ten happens to match.

choices.text: It finds every CPF and nothing else
choices.why: Any column with one stray match is labelled too, real or not.

choices.text: Scans refuse to run below 60 per cent
choices.why: The threshold is exposed exactly so that it can be set.

choices.text: False labels on chance matches
choices.why: Right. A threshold trades missed data against false labels; no setting removes both.

choices.text: Nothing changes, because the validator removes false matches
choices.why: About one random eleven-digit number in a hundred passes the CPF check digits.

prompt: A CPF's last two digits are ___ digits, computed from the nine before them.
hint: They let a typo be caught.

prompt: What is the difference between a classification and a sensitivity label?

choices.text: A classification is manual and a label is automatic
choices.why: Both can be applied automatically by a scan's rules.

choices.text: They are two names for the same thing
choices.why: "Holds CPFs" and "Confidential: personal data" say different things.

choices.text: Content versus policy
choices.why: Right. A classification says what the column holds; a label says how to treat it.

choices.text: Labels exist only for Microsoft 365 files, never for data assets
choices.why: The Data Map can apply them to scanned assets, as an option the organisation turns on.

prompt: A table carries "Confidential: personal data" in the catalogue. An analyst queries it in Azure SQL Database. What stops the analyst reading the CPF column?

choices.text: The label, which the database reads before each query
choices.why: The label is information in the catalogue; the store decides access.

choices.text: Purview, which intercepts the query
choices.why: Purview is not in the path of a query.

choices.text: The database's own permissions and masking, if somebody set them
choices.why: Right. The label informs whoever searches; enforcement lives in the store.

choices.text: The scan, which removes the column
choices.why: A scan reads; it never changes the source.

prompt: The Delta table written by `classify.py`'s cousin, a hand-written Python script, appears in the Data Map with no parent. Why?

choices.text: Its storage account was not scanned
choices.why: It was: the table is in the map; only its origin is missing.

choices.text: Nothing reported where its data came from
choices.why: Right. Lineage is reported by tools such as Data Factory; a script reports nothing.

choices.text: Delta tables cannot have lineage
choices.why: Any asset can have edges; this one simply got none.

choices.text: Purview reads lineage from the data, and the script's data was encrypted
choices.why: Purview does not discover lineage by reading data.

prompt: Match each part of Purview to what it adds.
hint: One describes, one prescribes, one traces, one lists.

pairs.right: assets and columns in the Data Map
how the data should be treated
lineage edges for copies and data flows

prompt: Which of these does a scan NOT produce?

choices.text: Assets in the Data Map
choices.why: That is what a scan writes.

choices.text: Classifications on columns
choices.why: A scan applies its rule set's classifications.

choices.text: An owner and glossary definitions
choices.why: Right. Curation is people's work, and a catalogue without it is a scan with a search box.

choices.text: Column names and types
choices.why: A scan reads a source's structure.

prompt: At the lesson's illustrative 0.60 USD per vCore-hour, a weekly scan of the lake using 4 vCore-hours replaces the nightly one. What do the scans cost in a month of 4 weeks, in USD?
Why does the lesson suggest one Purview account for the company rather than one per team?
hint: Which part of the bill does not depend on use?

choices.text: Each account's map pays at least one capacity unit every hour, used or not
choices.why: Right. The map is the fixed cost; scans are the variable one.

choices.text: Accounts cannot share a storage account
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so, and it is not the reason given.

choices.text: Scans are free in the first account
choices.why: Scans are billed by processing in every account.

choices.text: Lineage cannot cross accounts
choices.why: The lesson's reason is the fixed cost of the map.

prompt: Put in order how a CPF column in Quitanda's lake becomes a labelled asset in the catalogue.
items: The lake is registered as a source in a collection
Purview's identity is granted Storage Blob Data Reader on it
A scan reads a sample of each file
The CPF classification passes its threshold on the column
A labelling rule applies "Confidential: personal data" from the classification

prompt: Which of these did this lesson actually run? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A classifier of the course's own over an export in Azurite
choices.why: Right; `classify.py`.

choices.text: Terraform validating a Purview account declaration
choices.why: Right, offline.

choices.text: A Purview scan of Azurite
choices.why: Nothing of Purview ran.

choices.text: Lineage reported by Data Factory
choices.why: Documented, not run.

choices.text: A sensitivity label applied to a column
choices.why: Documented, not run.

prompt: A new team writes customer data to the lake with a nightly Python script and asks for it to be "in Purview". What will Purview know about the files after the next scan?
hint: Scans find and recognise; tools trace.

choices.text: Their columns and classifications, and no lineage
choices.why: Right. The scan fills the map; the script reports no edges unless the team adds them.

choices.text: Everything, including which tables the script read
choices.why: Reading the files does not reveal what produced them.

choices.text: Nothing until the script is rewritten in Data Factory
choices.why: The scan finds and classifies the files whatever wrote them.

choices.text: Their owner and glossary terms, taken from the script's comments
choices.why: Curation is people's work; scans read data, not comments in code.
